cards.front: muscle
cards.back: A body part that gets shorter (contracts) to pull on a bone and make it move.
cards.say: muscle. A body part that gets shorter (contracts) to pull on a bone and make it move.

cards.front: joint
cards.back: A place where two or more bones meet. Joints let the body bend and turn.
cards.say: joint. A place where two or more bones meet. Joints let the body bend and turn.

cards.front: tendon
cards.back: A strong cord that joins a muscle to a bone.
cards.say: tendon. A strong cord that joins a muscle to a bone.

cards.front: contract
cards.back: When a muscle gets shorter and thicker.
cards.say: contract. When a muscle gets shorter and thicker.

cards.front: relax
cards.back: When a muscle goes back to its longer, softer state.
cards.say: relax. When a muscle goes back to its longer, softer state.

cards.front: Why do muscles work in pairs?
cards.back: A muscle can only pull, not push. One muscle pulls the bone one way and the other pulls it back.
cards.say: Why do muscles work in pairs? A muscle can only pull, not push. One muscle pulls the bone one way and the other pulls it back.

cards.front: Which muscle contracts to bend your arm at the elbow?
cards.back: The biceps, at the front of the upper arm.
cards.say: Which muscle contracts to bend your arm at the elbow? The biceps, at the front of the upper arm.

cards.front: Which muscle contracts to straighten your arm?
cards.back: The triceps, at the back of the upper arm.
cards.say: Which muscle contracts to straighten your arm? The triceps, at the back of the upper arm.

cards.front: What does the triceps do when the biceps contracts?
cards.back: It relaxes.
cards.say: What does the triceps do when the biceps contracts? It relaxes.

cards.front: Can a muscle push a bone?
cards.back: No. Muscles can only pull.
cards.say: Can a muscle push a bone? No. Muscles can only pull.

cards.front: What is a pair of muscles that work together called?
cards.back: An antagonistic pair, with one pulling and one pulling back. Biceps and triceps are an example.
cards.say: What is a pair of muscles that work together called? An antagonistic pair, with one pulling and one pulling back. Biceps and triceps are an example.

cards.front: hinge joint
cards.back: A joint that moves back and forth like a door, such as the elbow or knee.
cards.say: hinge joint. A joint that moves back and forth like a door, such as the elbow or knee.

cards.front: ball and socket joint
cards.back: A joint that moves in many directions, such as the shoulder or hip.
cards.say: ball and socket joint A joint that moves in many directions, such as the shoulder or hip.

cards.front: Which joint lets your leg swing in a circle?
cards.back: The hip, a ball and socket joint.
cards.say: Which joint lets your leg swing in a circle? The hip, a ball and socket joint.

cards.front: Which joint bends like a door?
cards.back: A hinge joint, such as the knee.
cards.say: Which joint bends like a door? A hinge joint, such as the knee.

cards.front: What would happen if you had no joints?
cards.back: Your skeleton could not bend, so you could not move easily.
cards.say: What would happen if you had no joints? Your skeleton could not bend, so you could not move easily.

cards.front: cartilage
cards.back: A smooth, bendy material at the ends of bones that stops them rubbing.
cards.say: cartilage. A smooth, bendy material at the ends of bones that stops them rubbing.

cards.front: ligament
cards.back: A strong band that holds bones together at a joint.
cards.say: ligament. A strong band that holds bones together at a joint.

cards.front: Why does the knee have cartilage?
cards.back: It cushions the bones and lets them move smoothly.
cards.say: Why does the knee have cartilage? It cushions the bones and lets them move smoothly.

cards.front: What makes your bones move?
cards.back: Muscles pulling on them through tendons.
cards.say: What makes your bones move? Muscles pulling on them through tendons.

cards.front: Are muscles in the heart?
cards.back: Yes. The heart is a muscle that pumps blood.
cards.say: Are muscles in the heart? Yes. The heart is a muscle that pumps blood.

cards.front: How can you keep muscles strong?
cards.back: Exercise, eat protein and get enough rest.
cards.say: How can you keep muscles strong? Exercise, eat protein and get enough rest.

cards.front: True or false: Muscles attach to bones.
cards.back: True. Tendons join muscles to bones.
cards.say: True or false: Muscles attach to bones. True. Tendons join muscles to bones.

cards.front: True or false: A muscle pushes the bone back to its place.
cards.back: False. A different muscle pulls it back.
cards.say: True or false: A muscle pushes the bone back to its place. False. A different muscle pulls it back.
